kernels.name: authservice — identity as an image
kernels.description: A login service lifted out of a private monorepo and published as a versioned {{term:ghcr}} image. The consumer pins a tag in configuration and has **no** source dependency at all.
readiness: One codebase, N independent instances, no shared root of trust
The job that publishes the image needs none of the secrets required for deployment
The pattern is written up as a proposed standard, with an explicit note that it rests on one data point
kernels.blocker: There is no tag at all. Six repositories pin a version of an image whose existence cannot be confirmed — so the pattern is documented and the artefact is not.

kernels.name: {{term:playhead|Record/replay cassette}}
kernels.description: Recording and replaying model calls at the {{term:ichatclient}} seam. 250 lines, one package dependency, {{term:hermetyczny|hermeticity}} enforced by an architecture test and a separate CI job that builds the kernel in isolation.
readiness: Already physically extracted into `kernel/replay/` with its own project file and its own tests
No domain vocabulary; neutrality is tested, not declared
The first consumer is named and justified: an evaluation harness without replay cannot tell a regression from randomness
kernels.blocker: The name is provisional and has not been checked against the package registry. Check it **before** publishing — changing the identifier after the first install is a breaking change.

kernels.name: {{term:servicedefaults|ServiceDefaults}} — the shared host core
kernels.description: Authentication against JWKS, database provider selection, rate limiting with a uniform 429 response shape, background migration after the server starts. Ten projects in the portfolio do the same thing; **four wrote it independently from scratch**.
readiness: The CogniSim version has its cleanliness enforced by an architecture test and a mechanical line limit in CI
The authservice version has the best worked-out background migration, with a readiness signal
The primates version has the richest web layer
kernels.blocker: **There is no single version you can lift out.** Four implementations have 188, 177, 169 and 101 lines of database provider selection alone, and every one of them is different. First decide which is the reference and write that decision down — then extract.

kernels.name: Judge calibration ({{term:kappa|Cohen's kappa}})
kernels.description: Agreement between an LLM judge and human labels: unweighted, linearly weighted and quadratically weighted kappa, with a bootstrap and a confidence interval, plus a **ceiling taken from the mutual agreement of a human panel**, computed before the judge is scored.
readiness: The arithmetic itself is neutral: it computes agreement over ordinal labels and nothing else
The only dependency to remove is an import of the collector's domain namespace for a percentile helper — **two calls**
The CopilotScope version is the richest: 340 lines with three weighting variants and a separate 'ceiling too low' verdict
The other two consumers already have their own, thinner implementations — consolidation here removes code rather than adding it
kernels.blocker: None of the three implementations has been run against real human labels. Extracting a library will not fix the fact that nobody has labelled a sample yet.

kernels.name: An OTLP decoder without the SDK
kernels.description: A hand-written protobuf reader plus decoders for traces, metrics and logs, with the field numbers verified against the official `.proto` files. It receives {{term:otel|OTLP}} without pulling in the whole SDK.
readiness: It reads the generic OTLP format and knows nothing of sessions or sensors — the neutrality here is structural
Two versions exist: 718 lines in copilot-scope and 1063 lines in hydro-scope; the newer one is a superset
Both have their own decoder tests, so the extraction starts with coverage
kernels.blocker: Two consumers is the minimum, not comfort. If one of these repositories is archived after the extraction, the library drops to one user and goes back inside.

kernels.name: {{term:runstore|Run store}} and comparison
kernels.description: It stores a **run**, not a single span, with idempotent ingest and scoring off the request path. The {{term:comparison|comparison layer}} reports medians and spreads and has no field for a best run.
readiness: The distribution arithmetic itself is a hundred per cent generic
The run record needs parameterising — today it carries the ceremony's domain fields
The same data shape arose independently as the permission gate's {{term:audit|audit trail}}
kernels.blocker: Do this only once K1 has **two actual** consumers on main. That is the {{term:wip|work-in-progress limit}} rule, not a preference.

kernelsRejected.name: ArtefactExtractor — pulling artefacts out of a transcript
kernelsRejected.reason: It knows what a PI objective, a cross-team dependency and a ROAM risk are. That is not a dependency you can parameterise — it is **the entire value** of the component. Extracting it would leave an empty shell.

kernelsRejected.name: QualityEngine — the session quality score
kernelsRejected.reason: Six weights are an opinion about what a good session with an assistant means. An opinion is not a library; published as a library, it immediately becomes somebody else's metric that you have to answer for.

kernelsRejected.name: Roslyn analysers
kernelsRejected.reason: They encode the specific P1–P15 principles of this constitution. Outside it, half the rules need reconfiguring and the other half make no sense. What is reusable is the harness that runs them, not the analysers.

kernelsRejected.name: ConfirmationTokenStore — the write gate
kernelsRejected.reason: The pattern is neutral and tempting, but today it has **one** consumer. A library with one user is a project moved into a different directory, paid for with a separate CI run and a separate release.

kernelsRejected.name: Blazor BFF with a token pair in the cookie
kernelsRejected.reason: The layer is good and repeatable, but its surface is one application's routes. What repeats is a pattern to describe in a guide, not code to package.

kernelsRejected.name: Architecture tests
kernelsRejected.reason: The mechanism is portable, but every assertion refers to one repository's assembly names. Distribute it as a template in a guide, not as a package.

duplications.problem: **{{term:kappa|Cohen's kappa}} implemented three times, in two languages.**

sideA.what: `Calibration/Agreement.cs`, 340 lines, three weighting variants and a bootstrap

duplications.resolution: A third copy sits in the evaluation harness (228 lines). Together, 618 lines computing the same statistic. **One library, two consumers who delete code the moment they take it** — this is kernel K3 and the cleanest consolidation in the whole portfolio.

duplications.problem: **The OTLP decoder written twice, in files with identical names.**

sideB.what: `Core/Otlp/` — 1063 lines in files with **the same names**

duplications.resolution: These two repositories share nine identically named `.cs` files. The newer version is a superset of the older one, so the direction is settled: lift it out of hydro-scope and wire it into copilot-scope. This is kernel K4.

duplications.problem: **{{term:servicedefaults|ServiceDefaults}} in eleven projects, four written independently.**

sideA.what: 169 lines of database provider selection, 166 lines of authentication

sideB.what: 145 lines of authentication and a separate migration layer, all of it done differently

duplications.resolution: Aspire generates this project in every new solution and nobody references it — it gets copied. The convenience of the template is the source of the largest duplication in the portfolio. This is kernel K2, and also the hardest one, because you have to **pick the reference version first**.

duplications.problem: **Eight repositories have a licence file carrying somebody else's copyright line.**

sideA.what: MIT with a name copied from another project

sideB.what: the same thing, the same line

duplications.resolution: It affects eight repositories. One of them is public today — but six of the rest are candidates for opening, so the defect will surface at exactly the moment it does the most harm. This is not eight typos, it is one template copied eight times: **one session, eight commits**, and it is the cheapest fix with a real legal effect in the whole map.

duplications.problem: The {{term:audit|audit trail}} and the {{term:runstore|run store}} are the same data structure.

sideA.what: The run record as a compliance function — who, when, with what permission

sideB.what: The run record as a research function — what, how much, with what result

duplications.resolution: The same shape arose twice for two different reasons. Kernel K5 merges both, but only after K1 has two consumers — because merging the store is weeks of work and merging the cassette is hours.

duplications.problem: Fly.io deployment scaffolding written again from scratch in six repositories.

sideA.what: `flyio/` with nine configuration files, an infrastructure analysis and a document about secrets

sideB.what: The same thing, six files, the same directory layout and the same two documents

duplications.resolution: Six infrastructure analyses and eight documents about secrets describe the same pattern. The configuration code has to stay per-repo, but **the documents should be one guide** — and that guide already exists in the constitution. Replace the six copies with a link.

duplications.problem: Sixteen `ci.yml` files and **no two of them are identical**.

sideB.what: The same thing, in a different order, with different action versions

duplications.resolution: The classic pattern: copy, then drift. One `workflow_call` in a hub repository and three lines in each consumer replace sixteen files that are ageing independently.

duplications.problem: The LaTeX book build chain assembled five times.

sideA.what: `main.tex` + a 291-line preamble + a Makefile + three workflows

sideB.what: The same structure, with the preamble grown to 447 lines

duplications.resolution: On top of that, three lighter variants in the decks and the articles. The preamble and the Makefile are one template repository plus `git subtree` — and the traps (the non-breaking space mapping, a missing language in `babel`) are already written up in both and **should not be discovered a third time**.

duplications.problem: {{term:mutation|Mutation testing}} configured three times, differently each time.

sideA.what: Ten analyser variants with a test that the mutant gets through

sideB.what: Four broken agent variants, each with an assigned scenario

duplications.resolution: The third version is in judge-worker. Here the duplication is **apparent and healthy**: this is a method, not code, and every domain needs its own mutants. At most, the description of the method belongs in a guide.

boundaries.title: runtime ⟂ source code
boundaries.reason: {{term:roslyn}} analysis works on source code, the replay harness on agent runs. A different moment in the cycle, a different artefact, **a different buyer**. Gluing them together gives a product you cannot describe in one sentence — and a product without one sentence has no buyer.

boundaries.title: production telemetry ⟂ test scenario
boundaries.reason: Session observability and the evaluation harness use the same words — judge, rubric, score — and measure something entirely different. There the unit is **a session that happened**, here **a scenario that was designed**. What they share is the {{term:kappa|calibration}} arithmetic, and that is all: any further shared code would be a coincidence.

boundaries.title: content ⟂ product
boundaries.reason: The book is a {{term:kernel|channel}}, not a product, and trying to turn it into a product damages it in both directions: it stops being citable and never starts earning. The book sells the library, the library sells the service — in that order and with no shortcuts.

boundaries.title: evidence system ⟂ kernel
boundaries.reason: An evidence system **consumes** a kernel and never defines it. The moment the shape of the library starts following the needs of one proving ground, the library stops being a kernel and the proving ground gains a dependency it did not want.

boundaries.title: tool ⟂ attestation
boundaries.reason: A tool that produces evidence and a service that attests to evidence are two different businesses. {{term:atestacja|Attestation}} means taking on liability, and liability needs a legal entity and insurance. You sell the tool, the client's auditor attests — the same functionality, no transferred risk.

openPaid.rule:
**Open** — what you run locally and what produces a file.
**Paid** — what remembers, compares, integrates with your systems and survives an audit.
This is the {{term:opencore|open core line}}, drawn inside one repository rather than between repositories.
openPaid.openRole: Role: channel, credibility, citability. No revenue — and that is how it is meant to be.
openPaid.paidRole: Role: revenue. A platform fee plus charging per run. Not {{term:perseat|per seat}}, not {{term:outcome|per outcome}}.
open: K1 · {{term:playhead|record/replay cassette}} — on {{term:nuget}}, a README with one claim
K3 · judge calibration — pure arithmetic, no domain
K4 · an OTLP decoder without the SDK
K0 · authservice — an image in {{term:ghcr}}, the pattern already proven
agent-eval-bench — the scenarios and the schema, not a service
CogniSim — the reference engine, without the memory layer
The books and decks — {{term:mit|CC-BY}}, in full

paid.name: Rehearsal
paid.what: Import from Jira and Azure DevOps, artefacts, a report. You pay for the input and for the memory, not for the engine.

paid.name: Evidence Pack
paid.what: Retention, the link between a run and the version of the roles and the model, an {{term:evidence|audit export}}. It answers 'prove it', not 'debug it'.

paid.name: A gate for the team
paid.what: Breach history, trends, per-repository policy, a management report. The analysers stay open.

paid.name: Workshops and rollout
paid.what: The scenario, the facilitation, a licence for the material. The shortest path to a first invoice and the only one that does not need a product.

pricingNotes: **Do not sell {{term:atestacja|compliance attestation}} without a legal entity and insurance.** A tool that produces evidence and a service that attests to evidence are two different businesses, and the move from the first to the second is irreversible and is not something you do by accident in the copy on a sales page.

**Marketing headline yes, invoice by runs.** The metric 'the independence nobody has counted' is persuasive precisely because the client does not count it today — and for exactly that reason you cannot {{term:outcome|invoice}} against it.

**Do not close the engine.** The risk of a one-person project with no customers being cloned is close to zero; the risk of a .NET enterprise bouncing off an AGPL-style licence is a certainty. This is not an ideological choice, it is a reading of the adoption precedent.
